[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Longest arithmetic subsequence** [LC 1027 · Longest Arithmetic Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-arithmetic-subsequence/){difficulty="Medium"}

An index can end many arithmetic subsequences, one per difference. The state cannot be the index alone: $[20, 1, 15, 3, 10, 5, 8]$ has a step of $-5$ and other steps ending at the same places. The previous element with the same difference is the predecessor, and a pair that has never been seen starts a sequence of length 2.

[Solved in full in @sec-lis-p3-arith.]{.card-link}
